question: Chlorination of alkane is an example of:

options.text: both addition and substitution chain reaction

solution:
The Correct answer is __**substitution reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chlorination of alkane** is a type of **free radical substitution reaction**.
 
• In this reaction, a **hydrogen atom** in the alkane is replaced by a **chlorine atom**.
 
• This type of reaction typically occurs in the presence of **UV light or heat**, which provides the energy necessary to break the **chlorine molecule (Cl₂)** into free radicals.
 
• The reaction proceeds through a chain mechanism involving three steps: **initiation, propagation, and termination**.
 
• In the **initiation step**, UV light causes the **homolytic cleavage** of chlorine molecules into two chlorine radicals.
 
• During the **propagation steps**, chlorine radicals react with the alkane, producing **alkyl radicals** and HCl, which then react with more chlorine molecules to continue the chain reaction.
 
• Finally, in the **termination step**, radicals combine to form stable products, thus ending the reaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **addition reaction**__

 __
 
• In an **addition reaction**, two or more molecules combine to form a larger molecule.
 
• These reactions are common with compounds containing **double or triple bonds**, such as alkenes and alkynes.
 
• An example of an addition reaction is the **hydrogenation of ethene** to form ethane.
 
 
 
• **rearrangement reaction**__
 
 
• A **rearrangement reaction** involves the reorganization of the structure of a molecule.
 
• An example is the **Wagner-Meerwein rearrangement**, where a carbocation undergoes a structural change to form a more stable carbocation.
 
• These reactions are typical in organic chemistry where a molecule's **skeletal structure** is rearranged.
